- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates upward price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if recent sentiment is bullish.  
- Model overestimates downward moves in the 10–15 day horizon — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is bearish.  
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — if price is trending sharply, model should not revert too quickly; allow 1–2 day lag in correction.  
- Forecast horizon 30d often misses late-stage momentum — if sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon, adjust final 5–7 days upward.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals, model should not overfit to recent noise — smooth out sharp swings in forecast.
